documented_probe: Exercises the tblite-skill multi-objective evolutionary optimization capability: the agent authors a deterministic stdlib-only NSGA-II CLI (fast non-dominated sorting, crowding distance, binary tournament, crossover/mutation with feasibility repair, external elitist archive, exact hypervolume) for two documented problem families: a bounded knapsack with (value, -weight) objectives and continuous problems with closed-form Pareto fronts (f2 = 1 - f1^2; 3-objective f3 = 1 - f1^2 - f2^2). The probe runs /app/nsga.py on three hidden params files (different seeds, sizes, including a 3-objective case) and independently recomputes objectives from the returned encodings (feasibility + exact/rtol match), checks mutual non-domination and exact hypervolume consistency, then applies per-problem quality gates: knapsack hypervolume >= 0.85x of an independent same-seed reference NSGA-II run; saddle IGD-to-analytic-front strictly below 0.9x the median of 5 random-search fronts of identical budget; triplane documented front property (mean|f1^2+f2^2+f3-1| <= 0.05, max <= 0.25, spans >= 0.6) — plus a static check that the core NSGA-II components exist.
notes: Medium: implement a complete NSGA-II from scratch in pure stdlib with strict reproducibility (single random.Random(seed) stream), exact objective recomputation, exact 2D/3D union-of-boxes hypervolume, and problem-specific quality gates. Nonzero rubric for reasoning_depth (dominance/crowding/archive/tournament design, closed-form front reasoning), debugging_ambiguity (no per-run oracle; only property-based grading with float tolerances), adversarial_inputs (hidden seeds/sizes and a 3-objective problem with a documented front property), hidden_case_generalization (three hidden param sets spanning all problem families; hardcoded visible fronts and single-objective optimizers fail), quantitative_correctness (exact knapsack objectives, exact hypervolume, IGD metric, tight thresholds). Low tool_breadth/resource_pressure: stdlib-only and sub-second-to-few-second runtimes.
